The diagnostic differences between Histiocytic medullary reticulosis and other candidate diseases, such as Miliary tuberculosis and Acute myeloid leukemia, also support this diagnosis.

Additionally, the presence of trilineage dysplasia and erythrophagocytosis in the bone marrow aspirate further supports this diagnosis. While the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings can also be seen in other diseases, such as Histiocytic medullary reticulosis and Miliary tuberculosis, the combination of these findings makes Acute myeloid leukemia a likely diagnosis.
